why: Both analyses recognise Halvard as already great, refuse Halvard Six and the student brand, and protect the shop channel, pricing and Listening Room, but Analysis 2 matches the key's per-player profit denominator and names both key-person transitions (CEO at 61, winding head retiring) as brutal facts. Analysis 2 also has the tighter verdict and shows more restraint in an explicit stewardship mode, whereas Analysis 1 adds more new seats, an unsupported East Asia expansion, a capital-return policy and a machine-hour denominator the key does not use.
